observation.visible_scene: A calm lake in a mountain valley under a clear blue sky. On the left, a golden-brown grassy hill slopes down to the waterline, dotted with dry shrubs and a few bare branches. Across the lake stands a long snow-streaked mountain ridge with jagged peaks. The still water mirrors the mountains, hills and sky, producing an inverted reflection that fills the lower half of the frame. A small cluster of dark trees and a tiny white building sit on the right shore, and a few thin reeds appear at the bottom-left foreground.
visible_changes: The water surface is not perfectly glassy: the reflected image of the snow-capped ridge and the brown hillside continuously shimmers and wobbles, with the white snow streaks in the reflection bending, breaking and re-forming slightly from frame to frame.

The reflected bare branches on the right and the reflected hill texture on the left likewise deform subtly, consistent with gentle ripples moving across the surface rather than any change in the real objects above the water.
The actual mountains, hills, sky, shoreline trees and building hold fixed positions and shapes throughout the excerpt; only their mirror images change.
The camera framing (horizon line, hill silhouette, mountain peak positions relative to the image edges, foreground reeds) stays essentially constant, indicating no noticeable pan, tilt or zoom.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the surface ripples (e.g. wind) is not visible and is not inferred.
Whether the clip is part of a longer continuous shot or was cropped from a moving-camera segment is unknown; within this excerpt the camera appears static.
Any motion before t=0 or after t=2.67s is unknown.
uncertain_details: The ripple/reflection changes are subtle; whether they represent a single traveling wave or random small disturbances cannot be determined from the sampled frames.
A very slight camera drift cannot be fully ruled out, but background landmarks show no clear relative shift, so camera motion is treated as negligible/uncertain.
